key_insight: Putting trainable nonlinear functions on the connections, rather than using physical devices only as scalar weights, makes analogue neural networks much more efficient for smooth continuous-control tasks.
engineering_relevance: This points to low-power hardware AI designs that can fit robotics, kinematics, and energy-control problems with far fewer nodes and connections, with a projected CMOS power of about 30 microwatts.
method: Use Kolmogorov-Arnold-style trainable nonlinear functions on links between nodes.
Implement the functions as analogue band-pass filters on field-programmable analogue arrays.
Compare performance on smooth regression/control tasks versus classification-like decision boundaries.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful transfer to hardware across roughly 35,000 connections with quantified fidelity, and shows stronger gains on smooth targets such as robotic kinematics, continuous control, and photovoltaic maximum-power-point tracking.
watch_item: The parameter-efficiency advantage is task-dependent and does not appear for classification-like decision boundaries, so the approach is not universally superior.
paper_title: Low-power analogue neural networks with trainable nonlinear connections for continuous control
